thread.title: Options Playbook Radio 221: You May Be Holding Onto Spreads Too Long

author: Brian Overby
title: Options Playbook Radio 221: You May Be Holding Onto Spreads Too Long
text:
Posted 14 hours ago by Brian Overby in Brokerage Information Are you holding onto your spreads too long? Listen to Options Playbook Radio 221: You May Be Holding Onto Spreads Too Long Huddle, up listeners! It's time for Brian and Mark to take on listener questions, including: Options question of the week: Earnings season in in full swing. Which names will dominate your options trading this week? 47% - AAPL 6% - GPRO 10% - CBOE Question from Imhad1: Is HMNY now the most option-like stock ever? Back to $.08 after reverse splitting up to $14. Crazy! Who would buy an option on this thing? Question from Ling: I've heard some educators say that you should never hold out for the max profit in an options spread trade because that means you held onto it too long. Is this the case? Do you agree? Thx and enjoying the handbook. Question from Flyguy: Hey what do you guys do with your long calendar spreads? Do you close out the short leg if the stock doesn't move then keep the long leg or just close the whole spread out? About Brian Overby As Senior Options Analyst for Ally Invest, Brian Overby is a widely sought-after resource for his option trading knowledge and market insights. He has contributed to numerous articles for the Wall Street Journal, Reuters and Bloomberg and has had numerous appearances on CNBC Fast Money and Fox Business News. A veteran of the financial industry since 1992, Brian continually seeks to improve the understanding of the retail investor. He has given thousands of option trading seminars worldwide, written hundreds of articles on investing, and is the author of the popular trading resource, The Options Playbook and it’s free, acclaimed companion site OptionsPlaybook.com. Prior to joining Ally, Brian was a senior staff instructor for the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) and managed the training department for one of the world's largest market makers, Knight Trading Group.
